info.title: Evictions API
info.description: Submit and track an eviction case for a rental property in any US state or DC. Evictions API is not a law firm and does not give legal advice. After a live case is submitted we engage a licensed attorney in the property's state for it; nothing is served on a tenant or filed in court until that attorney has reviewed the case, and the attorney serves and files through their own accounts while the case shows its status, documents, deadlines, messages and charges. Test mode is free, uses a fictional state (ZZ) and never touches a real tenant or court: a built-in sandbox reviewer approves test cases automatically once they enter review, and `POST /v1/cases/{id}/advance` moves a test case on one step at a time. A request in live mode on a server where live mode is off answers 403 `live_unavailable`. POST requests accept an `Idempotency-Key` header.

get.summary: Whether a jurisdiction is served, and its notice rules

200.description: Served status, `handling`, jurisdiction ids and the grounds. In live mode every US state and DC is served with `handling: "attorney_direct"`, `action: null` and, for each ground, `notice: null` and the facts intake requires (`requiredFacts`); anything else is `served: false`. In test mode (`handling: "automated"`) the sandbox jurisdiction answers with its notice rules for each ground.

post.summary: Sandbox only: move a test case on by one step. Runs the step the case is waiting for now (the sandbox reviewer's review, a service or filing update, or the end of the notice period on the case's own sandbox clock), or records the next court outcome as the sandbox reviewer. A live case (nothing about a real case is ever advanced automatically), or a case outside the sandbox jurisdiction, gets 409 `sandbox_only`; a draft, a case on hold or a finished case gets 409 `nothing_to_advance`, as does a step whose last try failed, until its automatic retry (`error.details.retryAt`). While the step is already being taken, the case is returned as it is. At most 60 a minute per organization (429 `rate_limited`)

SessionToken.description: A session token (`ess_...`) from `POST /v1/auth/signup` or `/v1/auth/login`, valid for 30 days. On the case, webhook, API key and organization routes it acts for the user's organization in the mode named by the `X-Evictions-Mode` header: `test` (the default) or `live`.

AttorneyToken.description: A user token (`eut_...`) of a verified attorney.

state.description: Position in the case lifecycle, for example `notice_review` or `filing_submitted`.

handling.description: Who does the legal work. Every live case is `attorney_direct`: a licensed attorney engaged for the case reviews it, serves the notice and files in court, and the platform records each step. Every test case is `automated`: the sandbox pipeline.

attorney.description: The attorney engaged for an attorney-direct case, once recorded. Null until then, and always null for a test case.

barNumber.description: The attorney's bar number in that state.

erased.description: Whether the details of the case were erased, which we do case by case on request. An erased case keeps its id, state, dates, deadline names and charges. In `data` the names and the address read `[erased]` (the state and county are kept) and every other fact is gone; `courtCaseNumber` is null; each document keeps its id and `contentHash`, its `filename` reads `[erased]` and downloading it answers 410 `erased`; messages read `[erased]`. Any request that would change the case answers 409 `erased`.

erasedAt.description: When the details were erased. Null for a case that was not erased.

contentType.description: Decided from the file's first bytes when it was stored, never from its name.

contentHash.description: SHA-256 of the document bytes. An attorney approval names these.

Charge.description: An amount owed to the platform for a case: the platform fee, or court or service costs passed on at cost. The attorney's legal fee is never a charge here: it is quoted separately and paid to the attorney.

Note.description: A message on a case, between the customer and the platform.

Filing.description: A submission to the court. Attorney-only.

rejectionReasons.description: The court's reasons, when it rejected the filing.

ServiceAttempt.description: One request to serve a document on one defendant. Attorney-only.

failureReason.description: The process server's reason, when service failed.

Attention.description: Whether the case needs the attorney: it is on hold, or a job for it failed for good after its last state change.

AttorneyCase.description: The case as its assigned attorney sees it. Each read is recorded in the audit log as `tenant_data_viewed`.

events.description: The full audit trail, including internal events.
